text: {"changed_files": ["lib/string.c"], "summary": "strncasecmp() decremented s1 instead of incrementing it, so it walked s1 backwards and compared the wrong bytes; changed `*s1--` to `*s1++`."}

{"changed_files": ["lib/string.c"], "summary": "Fixed strcspn() in lib/string.c to advance the scan pointer with ++p instead of --p, which made it walk backwards off the string and return wrong lengths."}

{"changed_files": ["lib/string_helpers.c"], "summary": "In string_get_size(), the loop reducing a >32-bit size decremented the exponent i instead of incrementing it, so large sizes got the wrong (out-of-range, 'UNK') unit; restored i++."}

{"changed_files": ["lib/string_helpers.c"], "summary": "In string_escape_mem, the per-byte loop read via `*src--` instead of `*src++`, so the source pointer walked backwards; restored the post-increment so escaping consumes input in order."}

{"changed_files": ["lib/string_helpers.c"], "summary": "Fixed inverted condition in string_unescape() so escape sequences are processed only when a character follows the backslash (src[1] != '\\0'), restoring correct unescaping and trailing-backslash handling."}
{"changed_files": ["lib/cmdline.c"], "summary": "In get_option(), skip the leading '-' with ++cur instead of --cur so negative numbers like \"-3\" in \"0-1,-3,6\" are parsed correctly."}

{"changed_files": ["lib/cmdline.c"], "summary": "get_options() stopped parsing after every range or comma-terminated number because the loop exit condition was inverted (`res != 1` instead of `res == 1`), so only a trailing number without a comma should end the parse."}

{"changed_files": ["lib/cmdline.c"], "summary": "memparse() dropped the 'G' suffix shift because `ret << 10;` was a no-op statement instead of `ret <<= 10;`, so mem=1G parsed as 1 byte and no memory was available for the KUnit kernel."}

{"changed_files": ["lib/siphash.c"], "summary": "In __siphash_aligned the leftover byte count was masked with sizeof(u64) - 2 instead of sizeof(u64) - 1, dropping the low bit of the tail length and corrupting hashes for odd tail lengths."}

{"changed_files": ["lib/siphash.c"], "summary": "Fixed __hsiphash_aligned computing the tail-byte count with mask `sizeof(u64) - 2` instead of `sizeof(u64) - 1`, which dropped the low bit and hashed the wrong number of trailing bytes for odd remainders."}
